_about: The Non-Marxists section of the archive: thinkers and leaders filed outside the Index of Marxists. Works are 'hosted' (a text in content/texts/<id>.txt, in the public domain) or 'link' (the Marxists Internet Archive or another site). Each person needs a group code from 'groups'.
intro: Filed outside the Index of Marxists: the philosophers and economists Marx worked from, the utopians and anarchists he argued with, the revisionists, and the leaders who governed in Lenin's name after him. Read them to know what Marxism answered.

groups.title: The Philosophers
groups.blurb: Spinoza, Kant and the Young Hegelians: the philosophy Marx came out of and broke with, outside Hegel himself.

groups.title: The Economists
groups.blurb: Classical political economy, the science Marx set out to criticise.

groups.title: The Early Socialists
groups.blurb: The socialists and revolutionaries before scientific socialism: the utopians Engels honoured and answered, and the insurrections of Blanqui.

groups.title: The Anarchists
groups.blurb: Marx's rivals in the First International and their successors.

groups.title: The Revisionists
groups.blurb: Socialism by gradual reform, inside the Second International.

groups.title: The Stalinist Line
groups.blurb: Stalin, and the two leaders who kept his model of party and state longest after Moscow turned from it in 1956: Enver Hoxha in Albania and Kim Il-sung in North Korea.

groups.title: The Chinese Line
groups.blurb: Mao Zedong, who led the Chinese revolution to power in 1949, and the leaders of the party after him, from Deng Xiaoping's reform and opening to Xi Jinping.

groups.title: National Liberation
groups.blurb: Leaders of anti-colonial revolutions who took up Lenin's name: Ho Chi Minh in Vietnam, Fidel Castro and Che Guevara in Cuba.

groups.title: The Yugoslav Road
groups.blurb: Tito, whose Yugoslavia was expelled from the Cominform in 1948 for going its own way, and the workers' self-management and non-alignment it took up afterwards.

people.name: Baruch Spinoza
people.role: Dutch philosopher, expelled from Amsterdam's Jewish community in 1656, whose Ethics identifies God with nature. Hegel held that every philosopher must begin from Spinoza.

works.title: The Ethics
works.subtitle: Ethica Ordine Geometrico Demonstrata
works.edition: Translated from the Latin by R. H. M. Elwes. London, George Bell and Sons, 1883–84.

people.name: Immanuel Kant
people.role: Königsberg philosopher whose critical philosophy set the problems that Hegel answered. A century later, Bernstein and the neo-Kantians called for a return to Kant.

works.title: The Critique of Pure Reason
works.edition: Translated by J. M. D. Meiklejohn. London, 1855.

works.title: An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment?
Fundamental Principles of the Metaphysic of Morals
works.subtitle: Also known as the Groundwork
works.edition: Translated by Thomas Kingsmill Abbott. London, 1873.

people.name: Ludwig Feuerbach
people.role: Young Hegelian who turned Hegel's philosophy into a materialism of man and nature. Marx's Theses on Feuerbach and Engels's Ludwig Feuerbach settle accounts with him.

works.title: Towards a Critique of Hegel's Philosophy
The Essence of Christianity
works.edition: Translated from the second German edition by Marian Evans (George Eliot). London, 1854.

works.title: Principles of the Philosophy of the Future

people.name: Bruno Bauer
people.role: Young Hegelian theologian and critic of the Gospels, Marx's teacher and friend in Berlin, whom Marx answered in On the Jewish Question and, with Engels, in The Holy Family.
people.note: His writings are linked in the German originals; no public-domain English translation is known.

works.title: Der christliche Staat und unsere Zeit
works.subtitle: In German

works.title: Die gute Sache der Freiheit und meine eigene Angelegenheit
works.subtitle: In German

works.title: Die Fähigkeit der heutigen Juden und Christen, frei zu werden
works.subtitle: In German. Marx answered it in On the Jewish Question

works.title: Was ist jetzt Gegenstand der Kritik?
works.subtitle: In German

people.name: Moses Hess
people.role: Philosopher and socialist who won Engels over to communism in 1842 and worked with Marx in the 1840s; later the author of Rome and Jerusalem (1862), an early work of Zionism.

people.name: Adam Smith
people.role: Scottish moral philosopher whose Wealth of Nations founded classical political economy, the starting point of Marx's critique.

works.title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations

people.name: Thomas Malthus
people.role: Clergyman and economist whose law of population Marx attacked as an apology for poverty.

works.title: An Essay on the Principle of Population

people.name: David Ricardo
people.role: Stockbroker and economist who carried the labour theory of value further than anyone before Marx.

works.title: On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation

people.name: Henri de Saint-Simon
people.role: French aristocrat who imagined a society run by industrialists and scientists. Engels counted him among the three great utopians.

works.title: Letters from an Inhabitant of Geneva

people.name: Robert Owen
people.role: Welsh mill-owner who ran New Lanark as a model factory town and founded communities in Britain and America.

works.title: Report to the County of Lanark

people.name: Charles Fourier
people.role: French critic of commerce and of 'civilisation' who planned cooperative communities, the phalansteries.

works.title: The Social Destiny of Man, or Theory of the Four Movements

people.name: Auguste Blanqui
people.role: French revolutionary who spent more than thirty years in prison for his conspiracies and insurrections; his followers fought in the Paris Commune.

people.name: Max Stirner
people.role: Young Hegelian whose The Ego and Its Own set the individual above every cause. Marx and Engels answered him at great length in The German Ideology.

works.title: The Ego and His Own
works.subtitle: Also translated as The Ego and Its Own
works.edition: Translated by Steven T. Byington, with an introduction by J. L. Walker. New York, Benjamin R. Tucker, 1907.

people.name: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
people.role: French printer who declared that property is theft and was the first to call himself an anarchist. Marx answered his System of Economic Contradictions with The Poverty of Philosophy.

works.title: System of Economical Contradictions, or The Philosophy of Poverty
General Idea of the Revolution in the Nineteenth Century

people.name: Mikhail Bakunin
people.role: Russian revolutionary who fought Marx for the First International and was expelled from it at the Hague Congress of 1872.

works.title: God and the State
works.edition: Translated by Benjamin R. Tucker, with a preface by Carlo Cafiero and Élisée Reclus. New York, Mother Earth Publishing Association, 1916.

people.name: Peter Kropotkin
people.role: Russian prince and geographer, the leading theorist of anarchist communism.

works.title: The Conquest of Bread
works.edition: English translation first published in London in 1906; this text follows the Vanguard Press printing, New York, 1926.

works.title: Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution

people.name: Emma Goldman
people.role: Lithuanian-born American anarchist, deported to Soviet Russia in 1919, who wrote of her disillusionment there.

works.title: Anarchism and Other Essays
works.edition: With a biographic sketch by Hippolyte Havel. New York, Mother Earth Publishing Association, 1910.

people.name: Eduard Bernstein
people.role: Engels's literary executor, who argued from 1896 that socialism would come by gradual reform. His party rejected the revision, and Luxemburg answered it in Reform or Revolution.

works.title: Socialism in the German Reichstag and on the German Throne
Evolutionary Socialism
works.subtitle: Die Voraussetzungen des Sozialismus und die Aufgaben der Sozialdemokratie

people.name: Joseph Stalin
people.role: General Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party from 1922 and ruler of the USSR until his death in 1953; author of the doctrine of socialism in one country.
people.note: Linked, not hosted: the English translations here are not clearly in the public domain everywhere.

works.title: History of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (Bolsheviks): Short Course
Economic Problems of Socialism in the USSR

people.name: Enver Hoxha
people.role: Leader of Albania from 1944 until his death in 1985, who broke in turn with Yugoslavia, the Soviet Union and China.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

people.name: Kim Il-sung
people.role: Leader of North Korea from its founding in 1948 until his death in 1994, and author of its state doctrine of Juche.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

works.title: On the Establishment of the Workers' Party of North Korea
On Eliminating Dogmatism and Formalism and Establishing Juche in Ideological Work
The Great Anti-Imperialist Revolutionary Cause of the Asian, African and Latin American Peoples Is Invincible
For the Development of the Non-Aligned Movement

people.name: Mao Zedong
people.role: Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, who led it to power in 1949 and ruled the People's Republic of China until his death in 1976.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

people.name: Deng Xiaoping
people.role: Leader of China from 1978 into the 1990s, who opened its economy to the market under the name of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

works.title: Emancipate the Mind, Seek Truth from Facts and Unite as One in Looking to the Future
We Can Develop a Market Economy under Socialism
Building a Socialism with a Specifically Chinese Character

people.name: Xi Jinping
people.role: General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party since 2012 and President of China since 2013. His doctrine is written into the party constitution as Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the published English texts on other sites.

works.title: Report to the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China
Report to the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China

people.name: Ho Chi Minh
people.role: Founder of the Indochinese Communist Party in 1930, who declared Vietnam's independence in 1945 and led North Vietnam until his death in 1969.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

works.title: Some Considerations on the Colonial Question
Report on the National and Colonial Questions at the Fifth Congress of the Comintern
Declaration of Independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam

people.name: Fidel Castro
people.role: Lawyer who led the Cuban revolution of 1959, declared it socialist in 1961 and governed Cuba until 2008.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

works.title: At the Closing Session of the Tricontinental Conference

people.name: Che Guevara
people.role: Argentine doctor who fought in the Cuban revolution, ran Cuba's national bank and its ministry of industry, and was killed in Bolivia in 1967 while leading a guerrilla campaign.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

works.title: At the Afro-Asian Conference in Algeria

people.name: Josip Broz Tito
people.role: Leader of the Yugoslav partisans in the Second World War and of Yugoslavia from 1945 until his death; he broke with Stalin in 1948 and helped found the Non-Aligned Movement.
people.note: In copyright: these links open the Marxists Internet Archive.

works.title: Concerning the National Question and Social Patriotism
Letter to the Twentieth Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
Speech at the First Congress of Workers' Councils
